verdict_reasons: Agent produced a legitimate Revideo implementation of bouncing squares that rendered successfully to 433 frames at 18s duration
Scoring is multiplicative: gated_ssim (0.0003) * phash_similarity (0.0833) * duration (1.0) = 0.0, correctly reflecting poor visual similarity
Mean SSIM of 0.7204 barely exceeded the 0.70 gate, but cubic scaling above the gate yielded only 0.0003
Positions diverge massively after ~10 frames due to incorrect bounce physics (simple reflection vs 3-phase wall-shrinking)
No anti-cheat triggers, no reward manipulation, clean strace log
outcome_detail: Agent built a working bouncing-squares animation matching duration and initial positions, but used simplified constant-boundary bounce physics instead of the required 3-phase wall-shrinking dynamics. Positions diverge to 100-370px error by frame 200, yielding mean SSIM 0.7204 (gated to 0.0003) and phash similarity 0.0833.
strategy: Frame extraction, color tracking, velocity fitting, simple bounce physics
agent_behavior: Extracted all 433 reference frames and tracked 12 colored squares using Python/NumPy color detection scripts
Fitted per-square velocities via linear regression on frames 1-8 and refined with tighter tolerances
Read Revideo documentation (positioning, signals, tweening, flow) to learn the API
Built bouncing simulation using tween() with mathematical bounce function (modular arithmetic reflection)
Iterated on square size (60->48px), grid positions, and velocity parameters across multiple render cycles
Compared output vs reference at multiple frames, achieving <3px error for early frames but 100-370px error at later frames
Spent ~21 minutes on task execution, completing 5+ render-compare-adjust cycles
Failed to identify the 3-phase wall-shrinking behavior that fundamentally changes bounce boundaries over time
